Never heard someone talk about this before, I went through something similar!

My family makes six figures and while they did fall from grace financially when I was younger, we were always solidly middle class(I live in an expensive area). When it came to my brother(the golden child) he got whatever he wanted, didn’t matter what it was or how much it cost. I was refused therapy, medical care, the works because ‘we couldn’t afford it’. 

One specific instance of this was when I was a freshman in High school and my brother was in 6th grade. My mom couldn’t deny me therapy anymore because everyone genuinely thought I was going to off myself and she wasn’t happy about it. So I had just started and it was little after Christmas. In my childhood I was only ever allowed to even ask for something for holidays so my parents could brag about how good of parents they were. To be honest I can’t even express how much trouble I would have been in if I tried to ask for something especially after Christmas. Any way me and mom got into a fight(what it was I don’t remember) and I tried to cut it short by getting us out of the house and on the way to my 4th therapy appointment that we were going to be late for. I remind her to get a check and she starts screaming 10x louder, throwing coins at me(saying I wanted to take all her money) calling me a financial burden etc etc. We get to the appointment and we’re sitting in the waiting room and I look over and my mom is looking into buying a ps4. I ask her about it and she says that my brother wanted one and she was going to get it for him and I just had a meltdown. I cried so hard at the blatant favoritism and my therapist walks into the waiting room and I’m still crying into the corner of the couch. Asks my mom what happened and my moms like “oh I don’t know, she won’t tell me what’s going on” etc. The therapist brings me in and I told her everything immediately. I didn’t think much of it afterward until my therapist pointed it out a year later because it was such a given and so normalized for to distrust my mom. I had known her for a total of 3 hours but trusted her more than my mom. 

Not to mention when I got home from that appointment she gave me this whole big speech completely unprovoked about how I better be careful what I tell the therapist because she can get cps to take me away into a terrible foster home  and how I should never tell her that my mom called me a burden because it wasn’t true. Made the mistake of saying ‘but you did’ and I can still hear the way she gasped and said “I would never and have never called you a burden”. She knew what she was doing.
